The test image shows a split corn stalk with tan/golden-brown fibrous internal tissue and some white/bleached areas. This is clearly a stalk disease. Key candidates: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Gibberella_Disease, Fusarium_Disease, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot.

Let me view reference images one at a time.
Charcoal Stalk Rot shows dark gray pith with black sclerotia. Test image is more tan/golden without dark sclerotia. Check Diplodia next.

Excellent match! Charcoal_Stalk_Rot Corn_Disease_32 is very similar to the test image — split stalk on dark background, tan/golden fibrous interior with white center. Let me check Diplodia and Anthracnose to confirm.
Now I need to cover more unique classes. Let me check 6 more quickly:

All 16 views complete. 

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Split corn stalk on dark background showing tan/golden-brown fibrous internal tissue with white/cream central vascular region.
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot (Corn_Disease_32)**: Near-identical match — same dark background, same split stalk presentation, same golden-tan fibrous interior with lighter white center, same overall scale and framing.
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot (Corn_Disease_18)**: Also a split stalk view but with slightly darker/grayer pith and field background — less similar but still the same class.
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot**: Shows exterior features (hollow stalk, pycnidia dots), not the fibrous interior split view seen in the test image.
- **Fusarium/Gibberella**: Ear diseases, not stalks.
- **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot**: Black spots on green stalk exterior.
- **Bacterial_Stalk_Rot**: Exterior wilting.
- All leaf diseases (Rust, Tar Spot, NLB, etc.): Completely different morphology.

The test image is essentially the same type of photo as Charcoal_Stalk_Rot/Corn_Disease_32 — a cross-sectional fibrous stalk split on a dark studio background.
